attempts.label: DANDI:001260
attempts.paper_title: A prefrontal cortex map based on single-neuron activity
attempts.entry_title: A prefrontal cortex map from single-neuron activity (Le Merre, Heining et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Here is the paragraph so it can be saved as that file: Most descriptive findings hold up in this data, but the hierarchy findings could not be tested and two cross-region claims did not reproduce. Wide and narrow waveform classes, higher rates in narrow-spiking units, regular firing in prefrontal cortex, stable firing categories over time, and prefrontal subregion maps all reproduced. Correlations of firing categories with the cortical hierarchy, and the ILA-specific activity module, stayed undecided because the paper gives no rule for numbering categories on a retrained map. The match between narrow and wide units across regions and the high-rate tone-responsive result did not reproduce. The replication on International Brain Laboratory data was too large to attempt.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) on dandiset 001260, which holds 74 of the 99 Neuropixels recordings of the paper's dataset KI (the other 25 are in dandiset 000473). It recomputes the spontaneous firing metrics, the self-organizing map categories, their stability and their enrichment across brain regions, layers and the PFC flatmap, the Harris and Gao hierarchy correlations and the tone-response categories. The claims on the International Brain Laboratory data are not tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) from dandiset 001260

outcomes.notes: On 001260 + 000473 (the paper's 99 recordings), reading (b) with at least 6 spikes in at least 12 spontaneous epochs gives 24,898 units (24,248 ± 2,425), 52.4% in the PFC (52 ± 5.2) and 13,040 PFC units (12,674 ± 1,267). Every other epoch rule under reading (b) is within tolerance too (25,929, 23,168 and 22,091 units; 13,559, 12,026 and 11,509 PFC units); with the paper's Zenodo quality flags 24,270 units remain. Reading (a) of the files' undescribed quality columns gives 6,561 or 16,545 units. 001260 alone holds 74 recordings and 17,205 units, 47.3% PFC.
deviations: The counts use dandiset 000473 as well, as the criterion allows; 001260 alone holds 74 of the 99 recordings.

Assumption. The files carry no quality label; reading (b), all units, is the main one, as the paper's own flags on Zenodo pass 97% of units. The epoch rule is the Methods' unit quality control ("≥4 ISIs in at least 12 separate 3-s epochs", not restricted to active epochs) with the Methods' "at least six spikes (corresponding to at least four ISIs)"; 5 spikes, and active epochs only, are variants, and all give counts within tolerance.

Assumption. Sleep-like periods are detected per recording session from the pooled 10-ms counts of the cortical units of all its probes (Methods, Detection of sleep-like periods, "detected per recording session ... across all cortical spikes"), and not at all in a session where the detector marks 1% of the time or more in a Poisson population of the same pooled rate (10 sessions of 001260, among them the four probes the code marks "ignore"), a rule of this attempt and not of the paper; the Methods say detection "was only performed for the dataset KI, as sessions of this dataset consistently featured a sufficient number of cortical units to detect collective off periods", which describes no skipped session, and the rule was chosen because the paper's own detection files mark 19 recordings off_used = no. The per-probe detection of round 1, the code's detector, the main detector without detection in the sessions the paper's files mark off_used = no, and the paper's own sleep-like periods (Zenodo) are variants.

outcomes.notes: On 001260 + 000473, reading (b), at least 6 spikes in 12 spontaneous epochs, there are 19,731 ww (19,186 ± 1,919), 4,247 nw (4,200 ± 420) and 920 unclassified units (862 ± 86); ww are 79.2% and nw 17.1% of all units (82.3% and 17.7% of ww plus nw). With 5 spikes the unclassified units are 951, just outside; with active epochs only the ww units are 17,239, just outside; with the paper's Zenodo quality flags all three counts are within tolerance (19,182, 4,181, 907). The peak-to-trough histogram has modes at 0.26 and 0.64 ms and a minimum at 0.36 ms.
deviations: Peak-to-trough durations are the dataset's Peak_to_Trough column; they agree within 0.001 ms with the paper's Zenodo values for 95.1% of units.

outcomes.notes: PFC units are 49.4% of the 12,112 ww SOM units and hit all 425 nodes. Median B is -0.049 in PFC against -0.017 elsewhere (Mann-Whitney p = 5.3e-36); M < 0 in 56.0% against 69.3% (chi-square p = 1.5e-51). In the Aversion setting the B difference reverses (-0.076 against -0.096).

All 20,374 units of 001260 match a record of the Zenodo metrics files by recording and unit id. The location label agrees for 98.6% (283 differ, 207 of them in PL064_20200422-probe0) and the ww/nw label for 97.0%; peak-to-trough agrees within 0.001 ms for 95.1%. The paper's quality flags pass 19,808 units. All 9,408 units of 000473 have records too.

On dataset KI (001260 + 000473), 8,257 deep PFC ww units inside a subregion polygon give 39 dataROIs under either size bound (42 ± 4); the paper's tessellation on Zenodo has 42 polygons. On 001260 alone, 5,178 such units give 24 dataROIs, which the dataROI claims below use.
deviations: Uses 000473 for the count, as dataset KI is split across the two dandisets; the Zenodo flatmap positions are an outside input (zenodo-unit-link).

Units are assigned to subregions by the subregion polygons (code), which agree with the location label for 87.7% of units; within a subregion, to the nearest cluster center. The k-means seed is fixed (a standard choice).

Across 25 GaoROIs (29 in the paper), enrichment in responsive units does not correlate with the Gao hierarchy (r = 0.094, p = 0.65, or r = 0.023, p = 0.91).

Blocked because it depends on fig5g-tuned-unit-counts (dataset IBL). The dataset part was computed and is not reproduced on the 24 dataROIs of 001260: the tone-responsiveness map is most similar to spontaneous category 6 (G2 a) or 3 (G2 b), its cosine with category 8 is -0.13 to 0.12. On the paper's 42 dataROI polygons category 8 is highest in one of four readings (G1 a, G2 b, 0.19). No cosine exceeds 0.23.

The criterion fails under all 12 readings. Under G2 a the summed E-score of tone categories 1 to 7 is negative in spontaneous category 6 (-9.1 to -7.5); under G2 b it is negative in category 4 in five readings (-4.6 to -0.2), and in the sixth tone category 8 is positive in only 3 of the 5 low-rate categories. 4,123 units have both categories (6,681 expected for all of dataset KI).
Depends on fig5g-tuned-unit-counts and fig2i-ibl-replication (dataset IBL), not started.

The paper names no test. As a variant in the notebook, Metric ~ Setting + (1|Mouse) for ww units finds Detection different from Passive in log10FR (p = 0.04), Aversion in B (p = 0.0021), Context and Detection in M (p = 0.017 and 1.3e-05); marginal R2 0.008 to 0.035.

findings.statement: Dataset KI is split across two dandisets. 001260 holds 74 recordings, 41 mice and 20,374 units; the other 25 recordings (25 mice, 9,408 units) are in 000473, whose title and metadata name a different paper (Esr1+ hypothalamic-habenula neurons). Neither dandiset says it holds part of dataset KI.

The two dandisets hold 29,782 units, the paper's count before its unit quality control, and no field marks the 24,248 units the paper kept. The paper's quality flags are only in its Zenodo metrics files.

The units table's two-column `quality` is described only as "ISI violation, false positive rate". Column 0 runs from 0 to 1.15e5 (median 2), so it is not the ISI violation ratio of the Methods' threshold of 0.1, and its definition is not given.

The behavioral setting of a recording is not a field; it can be read only from the session description and keywords. The flatmap position of each unit and the paper's ww/nw labels are not in the files and come from the paper's Zenodo record.

In Detection and Context files the trials columns `lick` and `valve` are described as "sound amplitude"; in Detection files `Block` holds the trial outcome (miss, hit, correct rejection, false alarm), not a block. In a Context file `sound` is False for all 524 trials though 524 tones were played. Every electrodes column is described as "my description".

For 283 of 20,374 units the location label in the files differs from the paper's Zenodo metrics files (207 of them in PL064_20200422-probe0), and the ww/nw label from the paper's differs for 3.0% of units when the Methods' thresholds are applied to the files' Peak_to_Trough.

The Methods detect sleep-like troughs below 0.2 of the geometric mean for longer than 5 ms; the code requires off periods of more than 50 ms and at most 0.6 s, pads only groups of at least 3 off periods by 1 s, fills free gaps of 1.5 s or less, and uses only PFC units with at least 75 of them. Both give more sleep-like time here (median 9.9% per session-pooled detection, 8.7% for the code's) than the paper's 6%.

Following the Methods, sleep-like periods take a median 9.9% of each recording of 001260 (6% in the paper; per-probe detection gives 20.0%). The paper's own detection files on Zenodo give a median 5.3% over 73 recordings and mark 19 recordings as not using the detection (off_used = no), a selection step the Methods do not describe; where the paper used it, the Methods detector marks a median 15.9% of the time here.

The Methods require "≥4 ISIs in at least 12 separate 3-s epochs" for unit quality and compute burstiness and memory in epochs "with at least six spikes (corresponding to at least four ISIs)", though six spikes give five ISIs. The Methods also say 99 probes were lowered and 24 recordings excluded, while Data availability gives 99 recorded sessions, the number the two dandisets hold.

Question for the authors. The paper numbers its spontaneous categories by its own Ward clusters (code, a memory ranking and a fixed permutation) and describes them in words; it gives no rule that carries the numbering to a retrained SOM. Under the code's rule and under a match to the text's descriptions the outcomes of 8 enrichment and hierarchy claims differ, and they are blocked. Projected on the paper's own trained SOM (Zenodo SOMs.zip), the units take categories that match the text, and 4 of the 8 claims hold. Should a reanalysis project units on the trained SOM, or which rule should it use?

Question for the authors. Which test supports "firing metric distributions were not significantly different across behavioral settings"? A mixed model with setting as a fixed effect finds differences here (for example Aversion against Passive in B, p = 0.0021).

Question for the authors. Which recordings had an inherent block structure for the stability analysis, and how is it stored in the files? The Block column holds block numbers in some settings and the trial outcome in Detection.

Question for the authors. The Methods say all sleep-like periods were reviewed visually; the paper's detection files (Zenodo quiet_active_detection.zip) mark 19 of 73 recordings off_used = no. What decided that a recording's detection was not used, and should a reanalysis repeat it from the EMG and LFP in the files?

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested epoch_metrics, escore, stability, coincidence and the sleep-like detector on synthetic inputs and checked the archive for the blocked claims. Report in transcripts/001260/verifier-1-report.md. Its other points: E-score significance is a 10% two-sided test (now said in the notebook); REML Wald tests in place of Kenward-Roger (unchanged, stated); the 425-node grid and the PCA variance (stated; 95.1% now).

disagreements.reason: Under the main rule (12 active epochs of at least 6 spikes) there are 20,354 units and 10,900 PFC units, both outside tolerance. The Unit quality control passage, the claim's own source, says "≥4 ISIs in at least 12 separate 3-s epochs" and does not say active; under that reading all four values hold.
The mean r between ww 1-3 and nw 5 is -0.001 to -0.077 under every G1 and G2 reading. 21 regions were used; the paper used 9.
Category 2 r is -0.17 under G2 (a), and 0.39-0.40 (p ≥ 0.135) under G2 (b). It is not significant under any reading. 15 areas were used; the paper used 17.
No category has p < 0.05 across the 11 PFC subregions under any reading. With n = 11 this is a weak claim of absence.
Both ILA dataROIs share a module, but that module holds 2 of 6 ILA dataROIs, so it fails both "ILA-specific" readings. This uses only 22 dataROIs, 2 of them in ILA.

Under G2 (b), ROIs 20 and 41 are in the top three. Under G2 (a), ROI 23 is lowest in 3 of 4 combinations of reference and G1. Reference (b) with G1 (b) and G2 (a) gives not reproduced, so strictly G2 disagrees in that one combination. The Gao table's highest scores are ROIs 5, 24, 3, 2, not 19, 20 and 41.
No ORBvl dataROI is significantly enriched in tone category 1 under any of the 8 readings.
The tone-responsiveness map is most similar to category 1 under G2 (a) and to category 5 under G2 (b); both are the same cluster. It is never most similar to category 8. The IBL parts are untested.

entries.name: 001260-le-merre-2026
entries.title: A prefrontal cortex map from single-neuron activity (Le Merre, Heining et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) on dandiset 001260, which holds 74 of the 99 Neuropixels recordings of the paper's dataset KI (the other 25 are in dandiset 000473). It recomputes the spontaneous firing metrics, the self-organizing map categories, their stability and their enrichment across brain regions, layers and the PFC flatmap, the Harris and Gao hierarchy correlations and the tone-response categories. The claims on the International Brain Laboratory data are not tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) from dandiset 001260
